params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id (with roleIds) to derive member ids.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids.

params.name: memberIds
params.description: Explicit member ids (alternative to roleIds).

steps.example:

steps.name: agents.expectTeamCard
steps.description: UI: the team card and every member row are present on the Agents page. Member ids follow `<teamId>-<roleId>` and are unique text, so we assert on them directly (the team card is expanded by default).

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id shown on the team card.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids (`<teamId>-<roleId>`).

params.name: memberIds
params.description: Explicit member ids (alternative to roleIds).

steps.name: chat.expectTriggerFired
steps.description: Assert that a github-event TRIGGER woke this agent, observed on the session SSE stream (#711 — "trigger fired = the agent's chat shows the trigger event via SSE"). The runtime appends a `trigger.fired` event to the session log at the head of every triggered run (agent-entrypoint.py `_execute_inner`); we subscribe to that agent's session stream from byte 0 and resolve on it. Self- contained: resolves the agent's DM room id itself (the trigger posts there), so the journey YAML only names the agentId. The stream endpoint holds the connection open even before the log file exists, so subscribing right after applying the label is safe (no lost event, no sleep).

params.name: agentId
params.description: Id of the agent expected to be woken by the trigger.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait for the trigger.fired event.

steps.name: chat.open
steps.description: Open an agent's DM chat and wait for the composer to be ready.

params.name: agentId
params.description: Id of the agent whose DM chat to open.

steps.name: chat.send
steps.description: Type a message and send it via the Send control (the same path a human uses; plain Enter is a newline, the button is disabled until the text is non-empty).

params.name: text
params.description: Message body to type and send.

steps.name: chat.waitForAgentReady
steps.description: Wait until the agent's RUNTIME is demonstrably up before sending the first message. The runtime drops any m.room.message whose origin_server_ts predates its own process start (agent-entrypoint.py, `ts < start_time_ms`) — so a send that races the container boot is silently ignored BY DESIGN, and F2 would time out without any product bug. `/api/agents/statuses` flips the agent from `offline` to `idle` exactly when the runtime has booted and pushed its status.json (#185) — after that point, a fresh message is inside the processing contract. Bounded poll, no sleeps beyond the interval tick.

params.name: agentId
params.description: Id of the agent whose runtime to wait for.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait for readiness.

steps.name: env.createFixtureEnv
steps.description: Create a Working Environment pointing at the in-stack git-remote fixture repo. Credential-less on purpose: no sshKeyId, no githubTokenId — the orchestrator clones `http://git-remote/…` anonymously and the poller ignores a token-less env, so the team materialises with zero external dependencies.

params.name: id
params.description: Slug id for the new environment.

params.name: name
params.description: Human-readable environment name.

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at.

params.name: branch
params.description: Branch to track.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: env.createFixtureEnv
    id: agentic-demos-env
    name: Agentic Demos
    repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"

steps.name: env.createFixtureToken
steps.description: Create a GitHub token so the poller will poll the fixture repo (#711). The value is a syntactically-valid but fake PAT — the in-stack fake-github ignores auth entirely; it only needs to EXIST so `env.githubTokenId` resolves and the repo enters the poll plan. Idempotent via a fixed id (409 = already there).

params.name: id
params.description: Slug id for the token (referenced by the env).

params.name: name
params.description: Human-readable name.

steps.name: env.deleteEnv
steps.description: Idempotent teardown — 204 (deleted) and 404 (already gone) are both success, so a re-run or a partially-failed spec leaves no environment behind.

params.name: id
params.description: Id of the environment to delete.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: env.deleteEnv
    id: agentic-demos-env

steps.name: env.deleteFixtureToken
steps.description: Idempotent token teardown — 204 (deleted) and 404 (already gone) are success.

params.name: id
params.description: Id of the GitHub token to delete.

steps.name: flows.addAgentFromScratch

params.name: repo
params.description: "owner/name" of the repo on fake-github.

params.name: label
params.description: Label to apply (e.g. `ready`).

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait for the issue to appear.

params.name: repo
params.description: "owner/name" of the repo on fake-github.

params.name: bodyIncludes

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait.

params.name: hasLabel

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait.

steps.name: gh.expectPrExists

params.name: repo
params.description: "owner/name" of the repo on fake-github.

params.name: hasLabel
params.description: If set, require a PR carrying this label.

params.name: timeoutMs
params.description: Max time to wait.

steps.name: templates.expectTemplateCatalog
steps.description: Assert the template catalog: the New-template action, the ID/Category/Session/ Source columns, and a row for each expected built-in template. Capture point for the template-library screenshot (slide 35 of the walkthrough).

steps.example:
- assert:
    do: templates.expectTemplateCatalog
    templateNames: [Business Analyst, Developer, Code Reviewer]

steps.name: templates.openTemplatesPage
steps.description: Open the Agent Templates management page and confirm it rendered (its h1).
steps.example:
- action:
    do: templates.openTemplatesPage

steps.name: triggers.cancelForm
steps.description: Cancel the open Add-trigger form without saving (used for the github-event / data-flow form tour, which can't persist without a parseable repo in the E2E stack).
steps.example:
- action:
    do: triggers.cancelForm

steps.name: triggers.configureCron
steps.description: Configure a Cron (recurring) trigger: Daily at the given time + prompt. Opens a fresh Add form; does NOT submit (see module header). The plain-language summary and the underlying cron expression render in the form.

params.name: time
params.description: 24h HH:MM the daily schedule fires at.

params.name: prompt
params.description: The instruction the agent receives when it fires.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: triggers.configureCron
    time: "07:00"
    prompt: Generate a summary of the pull requests completed yesterday.

steps.name: triggers.configureDataFlow
steps.description: Configure a Data flow — agent dependency trigger: the "wake on any push" hand-off + prompt. Opens a fresh Add form; does NOT submit. `repo` is optional for the same reason as configureGithubEvent (the in-stack repo isn't a parseable github.com URL), so the journey tours the dependency note without a repo.

params.name: repo
params.description: "owner/name" repo the dependency is on (omit if none parseable).

params.name: prompt
params.description: The instruction delivered when an upstream push lands.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: triggers.configureDataFlow
    prompt: An upstream teammate pushed work — pull, check relevance, continue or reply [PASS].

steps.name: triggers.configureGithubEvent
steps.description: Configure a GitHub event trigger: optionally pick the repo, then the event, an optional label filter, and the prompt. Opens a fresh Add form; does NOT submit. Selecting the type loads the repo list from the agent's working environment — in the E2E stack the repo is served over the in-stack git remote (not a github.com URL), so the panel's github.com-only parser lists no repo; the journey therefore tours this form (event catalog + label filter) without a repo and does not save it. (github-event firing end-to-end is covered by iban-story.)

params.name: repo
params.description: "owner/name" repo to watch (omit if the env has none parseable).

params.name: event
params.description: Event key, e.g. "issues.labeled".

params.name: labelFilter
params.description: Exact label to fire on (labelable events only).

params.name: prompt
params.description: The instruction delivered when the event fires.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: triggers.configureGithubEvent
    event: issues.labeled
    labelFilter: ready
    prompt: A ready issue was labelled — pick it up and begin implementation.

steps.name: triggers.configureHttp
steps.description: Configure an HTTP webhook trigger + prompt. Opens a fresh Add form; a shared secret is auto-generated when the type is selected. Does NOT submit.

params.name: prompt
params.description: The instruction delivered when the hook is called.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: triggers.configureHttp
    prompt: The CI/CD pipeline has just deployed a new version to production.

steps.name: triggers.configureOnce
steps.description: Configure a Once (one-shot) trigger at a fixed future Date & Time + prompt. Opens a fresh Add form; does NOT submit. Use a fixed future timestamp for screenshot determinism (§7) — a one-shot in the future never fires mid-run.

params.name: at
params.description: datetime-local value, "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM".

params.name: prompt
params.description: The instruction delivered when it fires.

steps.example:
- action:
    do: triggers.configureOnce
    at: "2027-07-20T08:00"
    prompt: Remind me once that I am responsible for the time reporting this week.

steps.name: triggers.expectCronForm
steps.description: Assert the Cron form shows its plain-language summary and cron expression (capture point). e.g. summary "Every day at 07:00", expression "0 7 * * *".

params.name: summary
params.description: Plain-language schedule text to expect.

params.name: cron
params.description: The 5-field cron expression to expect.

steps.example:

steps.name: triggers.expectDataFlowForm

steps.name: triggers.expectOnceForm

steps.name: wizard.createTeamAndExpectProgress
steps.description: Journey-friendly wrapper: submit the wizard and assert the per-step NDJSON progress (plan lists team+members+dms, every step reaches `done`, complete carries the teamId + all members). Encapsulates the F1 inline assertions so a journey can express "create and verify" as a single step-library call. Accepts { teamId, memberIds } or { teamId, roleIds }.

params.description: Team slug id the complete event must carry.

params.name: roleIds
params.description: Role ids to derive member ids (`<teamId>-<roleId>`).

params.name: memberIds
params.description: Explicit member ids (alternative to roleIds).

steps.name: wizard.expectFlowPreview
steps.description: Assert the Process step's live flow preview + wiring check rendered lint-clean (StepProcess.jsx: "Flow preview — N agents" + "Wiring is clean"). Optionally spot-check the SERVER-derived rendering (#1009): the preview draws the same edge set as the Flows view, so a known edge label and its legend entry must be visible in the preview SVG.

params.name: edgeLabel
params.description: An edge label expected inside the preview SVG (e.g. the gate label).

params.name: legendEntry
params.description: A legend entry expected under the preview (e.g. "human approval").

- assert:

    edgeLabel: ready-for-implementation
    legendEntry: human approval

fixtures.name: flowsDraft
fixtures.description: flowsDraft: the `flows-draft` journey's precondition (#733). The journey authors a draft named `draftName` and never materialises it, so there is no team/env/Matrix state — only the draft document. This fixture just pre-/post- cleans any draft with that name so a re-run (or a crashed prior run) starts and ends clean.

params.name: draftName
params.description: Draft name the journey renames to.

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: flowsDraft
    params:
      draftName: Simple SDLC

fixtures.name: ibanStoryTeam
fixtures.description: ibanStoryTeam: the IBAN-story journey's precondition (#711). Stands up the WHOLE label-chain stack in one atomic precondition so the journey body only drives the hops: it (1) resets fake-github so the run starts from clean GitHub state, (2) creates a fake GitHub token so the poller actually polls the fixture repo (a token-less env is ignored by the poller), (3) creates a credential-carrying Working Environment pointing at the in-stack git remote, and (4) materialises a full Core SDLC team FROM THE PROCESS-TEMPLATE BUNDLE — so `POST /api/teams` runs `expandGithubChannels` and the Developer/Code-Reviewer get the derived github-event channel triggers (issues.labeled=`ready`, pull_request.labeled= `ready-for-review`) that carry the label chain. Bare `roles` would materialise the same agents WITHOUT those channels. FIXED ids keep the journey re-runnable on the same stack: setup pre-cleans any leftover team+env+token from a crashed prior run, and teardown removes the team, env and token this journey created — one deterministic, idempotent surface.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id to create (also its member prefix).

params.name: teamName
params.description: Team display name.

params.name: envId
params.description: Fixture environment id to create.

params.name: envName
params.description: Fixture environment display name.

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at (the in-stack git remote).

params.name: tokenId
params.description: Fixture GitHub-token id (referenced by the env).

params.name: branch
params.description: Branch to track.

params.name: templateId
params.description: Process template to materialise.

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: ibanStoryTeam
    params:
      teamId: iban-demo
      teamName: IBAN Demo
      envId: iban-demo-env
      envName: IBAN Demo
      repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"
      tokenId: iban-demo-token

fixtures.name: teamEnv
fixtures.description: teamEnv: the Team-Setup pilot's precondition. Seeds a credential-less Working Environment pointing at the in-stack git remote, so the wizard can materialise a team with zero external dependencies. Because the journey uses FIXED ids (for screenshot determinism, §7), setup first tears down any leftover team+env from a crashed prior run, and teardown removes the team this journey creates plus the fixture env — one deterministic, idempotent surface.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id the journey will create (pre-cleaned).

params.name: envId
params.description: Fixture environment id to create.

params.name: envName
params.description: Fixture environment display name.

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: Git URL the environment points at.

params.name: branch
params.description: Branch to track.

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: teamEnv
    params:
      teamId: agentic-demos
      envId: agentic-demos-env
      envName: Agentic Demos
      repoUrl: "http://git-remote/e2e/fixture.git"

fixtures.name: triggerAgent
fixtures.description: triggerAgent: the `triggers` journey's precondition (#733). Stands up ONE Business-Analyst agent to hang triggers on, as cheaply as possible: a credential-less Working Environment plus a single-member team. The env's repository URL is deliberately a github.com URL so the trigger panel's repo picker (parseRepoFullName, github.com-only) offers it for the github-event / data-flow trigger types — while the token-less HTTPS clone is refused fast by the orchestrator (no PAT ⇒ no username-prompt hang) and tolerated as a seed warning, so the member still materialises. No token ⇒ the poller ignores the repo, so nothing the journey configures ever fires: the config tour stays deterministic (github-event firing end-to-end is already covered by the iban-story journey). FIXED ids keep it re-runnable: setup pre-cleans a leftover team+env, teardown removes the team (cascades to the member) + env.

params.name: teamId
params.description: Team slug id (its BA member is `<teamId>-business-analyst`).

params.name: envId
params.description: Fixture environment id to create.

params.name: envName
params.description: Fixture environment display name.

params.name: repoUrl
params.description: github.com repo URL (parseable by the trigger repo picker).

fixtures.example:
fixtures:
  - fixture: triggerAgent
    params:
      teamId: triggers-demo
      envId: triggers-demo-env
      envName: Triggers Demo
      repoUrl: "https://github.com/aee-e2e/triggers-demo.git"
